content.title: About
content.content: Pizza with pepperoni and stuffed crust is a classic Italian‑style pizza topped with tomato sauce, mozzarella cheese, and slices of spicy pepperoni sausage. The crust is filled with a buttery cheese blend, making it extra juicy and crunchy.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pepperoni is an American version of Italian salami that became popular in the United States in the early 20th century.
Stuffed‑crust pizza was introduced in the 1990s as a way to add extra cheesy flavor without increasing the amount of cheese on top.
Traditional pizza is baked in a wood‑fired oven at 400–500 °C, giving it a distinctive aroma and crisp crust.
The combination of spicy pepperoni and a creamy cheese‑filled crust creates a flavor contrast loved by many fans of bold foods.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Pepperoni provides animal protein, which is essential for tissue repair and muscle maintenance.

items.title: Calcium from cheese
items.content: Mozzarella and the cheese filling are good sources of calcium, supporting bone health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The sausage and dough contain B1, B2, and B6 vitamins important for metabolism.

items.title: Energy dense
items.content: Pizza delivers a quick supply of calories, useful during periods of high physical activity.

items.title: Lycopene from tomatoes
items.content: Tomato sauce is rich in lycopene, an antioxidant that may support heart health.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Pepperoni and sauce often contain a lot of salt, which can be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: Cheese and processed meat are high in saturated fats, which may raise cholesterol when consumed in excess.

items.title: Dairy allergy or lactose intolerance
items.content: People with milk protein allergy or lactose intolerance should choose alternative options.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: A single slice can contain 300–500 kcal, so portion control is advisable.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Slice the pizza into even pieces and serve hot. Fresh basil or arugula can be added for brightness, and an extra sprinkle of grated Parmesan is optional.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2–3 days. Reheat in an oven or grill to keep the crust crisp.
